name: TerraMind 1.0 Tiny
description: On-demand 192-dimensional patch embeddings from the frozen TerraMind 1.0 Tiny encoder, computed from Copernicus Sentinel-2 L1C, Sentinel-1 GRD and Copernicus DEM at 10 m. The encoder is exported to ONNX once and runs through onnxruntime, so the openEO sandbox needs no PyTorch or TerraTorch.
warning: TerraMind is single-timestep: the process reduces each input collection to one temporal median composite before inference. The encoder sees 224x224 pixel tiles and produces a 14x14 grid of 16x16-pixel patch tokens, which are replicated back to the 10 m input grid; native spatial support is therefore about 160 m. TerraMind was pretrained on 224x224 S2 L1C input in raw digital numbers with its own mean/std. Sentinel-1 GRD is converted from linear power to decibels before inference, and Copernicus DEM values are used in metres. Embeddings depend on the selected composite, so a different temporal window yields different values.

parameters.name: spatial_extent
parameters.description: Area to compute embeddings for (WGS84 bounding box).

parameters.name: temporal_extent
parameters.description: Period to reduce to one composite before inference, e.g. one calendar year.

parameters.name: s2_bands
parameters.description: Sentinel-2 L1C bands in TerraMind order: coastal aerosol, blue, green, red, three red-edge bands, broad NIR, narrow NIR, water vapour, cirrus, SWIR 1 and SWIR 2.

parameters.name: dem_band
parameters.description: Digital elevation model band name, in metres.

parameters.name: max_cloud_cover
parameters.description: Maximum scene-level cloud cover (percent) for Sentinel-2 scenes used in the temporal composite.

publication.title: TerraMind: Large-Scale Generative Multimodality for Earth Observation
publication.citation: Jakubik, J. et al. (2025). _ICCV_. Accessed: 24 November 2026.
publication.abstract: We present TerraMind, the first any-to-any generative, multimodal foundation model for Earth observation (EO). Unlike other multimodal models, TerraMind is pretrained on dual-scale representations combining both token-level and pixel-level data across modalities. On a token level, TerraMind encodes high-level contextual information to learn cross-modal relationships, while on a pixel level, TerraMind leverages fine-grained representations to capture critical spatial nuances. We pretrained TerraMind on nine geospatial modalities of a global, large-scale dataset. In this paper, we demonstrate that (i) TerraMind's dual-scale early fusion approach unlocks a range of zero-shot and few-shot applications for Earth observation, (ii) TerraMind introduces "Thinking-in-Modalities" (TiM) -- the capability of generating additional artificial data during finetuning and inference to improve the model output -- and (iii) TerraMind achieves beyond state-of-the-art performance in community-standard benchmarks for EO like PANGAEA. The pretraining dataset, the model weights, and our code are open-sourced under a permissive license.
